title: 2013 HMMT November General Problem 8
statement: How many of the first 1000 positive integers can be written as the sum of finitely many distinct numbers from the sequence \(3^{0}, 3^{1}, 3^{2}, \ldots\) ?

solutions.text: 105 We want to find which integers have only 0's and 1's in their base 3 representation. Note that \(1000_{10}=1101001_{3}\). We can construct a bijection from all such numbers to the binary strings, by mapping \(x_{3} \leftrightarrow x_{2}\). Since \(1101001_{2}=105_{10}\), we conclude that the answer is 105 .
